messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: A higher Geriatric Depression Scale score was significantly associated with vitamin D deficiency in frail older hospitalized patients.
Sentence: "In a stepwise logistic regression analysis, only previous intake of vitamin D supplementation and high Geriatric Depression Scale score (GDS-15) were significantly associated with vitamin D deficiency."
Measured as: Geriatric Depression Scale score (GDS-15)
Population: 217 consecutively admitted frail older geriatric hospitalized patients, mean age 81.6 years, 70% female
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D measured at hospital admission; no intervention given
Comparator: Not applicable (observational association; vitamin D sufficient vs deficient patients)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 217
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D levels were significantly associated with postpartum depressive symptom scores (EPDS); direction not stated in the abstract.
Sentence: "Significant associations were identified between EPDS scores and the levels of estrogen, progesterone, thyroid hormones (TSH, FT3, and FT4), inflammatory markers (CRP and ferritin), vitamin D, and coagulation parameters (APTT and INR)."
Measured as: postpartum depressive symptoms (EPDS)
Population: 860 postpartum women recruited at hospital discharge (1-2 weeks after childbirth) at a tertiary hospital in Timisoara, Romania
Intervention: Blood vitamin D level (measured, not given)
Comparator: Across participants by vitamin D level
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 860
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are cross-sectional associations of vitamin D with depression scores, but Study B's abstract reports a significant association (direction unstated), so labeling it 'no effect' reflects extraction ambiguity; the populations (frail elderly inpatients vs postpartum women) and instruments (GDS-15 vs EPDS) differ.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["outcome_measure"],"detail":"population: frail hospitalized older adults (mean 81.6 y) vs postpartum women 1-2 weeks after childbirth; scale: GDS-15 vs EPDS"}
